title: The Carrion Market
text: A market opens at night in the boneyard. Its stalls sell teeth, hours, the second halves of letters, a mother's voice in a bottle. They take Gold. They would rather take something else.

options.label: Pay in Gold and keep your years for yourselves.

outcomes.text: You come away with a stoppered bottle the Apothecary cannot name, and a book with its last page torn out.
What you bought is gone by the time you get home. The receipt is in your own handwriting.

options.label: Pay in years, as they prefer; their wares are worth more that way.

outcomes.text: The Scion who paid wakes a decade older, but the bargain was good: a sliver of moonlight in a jar, real enough to forge.
The Scion who paid comes home older and forgetful. Whatever they knew of fighting, they must learn again.

options.label: Keep the House at home; nothing sold among the bones is worth buying.

outcomes.text: The music from the boneyard goes on until the dawn bell. Some of the tunes are ones your mothers sang.
